articles.title: Google Described Its Agent Sandbox. I Built One with Firecracker and Measured It
articles.summary: On October 22 Google described Agent Compute Engine : every AI agent session gets its own microVM, which is checkpointed while the model thinks, cloned copy-on-write from warm snapshots, and given no network card. You can’t use it yet, and the post has no latency or density numbers. So I built the same pattern on Firecracker in about 2,200 lines of Go and measured it on two machines. Sixty-four idle forks of a 512 MiB VM cost about 3 MiB of host memory each.
